32:4: The Almighty informs us that He is the Creator of all things, so He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then He established Himself on the Throne, and we have already discussed that. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. That is, He is the Owner of all affairs, the Creator of all things, the Disposer of all things, the Able to do all things. There is no protector for His creation other than Him, and no intercessor except after His permission. Then will you not remember? That is, you who worship other than Him and put your trust in anyone other than Him. He is exalted, sanctified, and far removed from having a peer, partner, minister, equal, or equal. There is no god but Him, and no lord but Him. Al-Nasa’i included a hadith here and said: Ibrahim bin Ya’qub told us, Muhammad bin al-Sabah told me, Abu Ubaidah al-Haddad told us, al-Akhdar bin Ajlan told us, on the authority of Abu Jurayj al-Makki, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: God created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, then He rose over the Throne on the seventh day. He created the soil on Saturday, the mountains on Sunday, the trees on Monday, the unpleasant things on Tuesday, the light on Wednesday, the animals on Thursday, and Adam on Friday in the last hour of the day after the afternoon prayer. He created him from the skin of the earth: its red and black, its good and bad. For this reason, God made the good and bad among the children of Adam.” This is how he included this hadith in its chain of transmission and text. Muslim and al-Nasa’i also included a hadith from Hajjaj bin Muhammad al-A’war, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayyah, on the authority of Ayyub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar context. Al-Bukhari explained it in his book, At-Tirmidhi. Al-Tarikh Al-Kabir said: Some of them said: Abu Hurairah on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and this is more authentic. And more than one of the hadith masters gave reasons for it, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, then it ascends to Him. That is, His command descends from the highest heavens to the furthest reaches of the seventh earth, as God the Almighty says: “God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends between them.” (Surah al-A’raf 7:10) And deeds are raised to their register above the lowest heaven, and the distance between it and the earth is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of the heaven is five hundred years. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: The angel’s descent is a journey of five hundred years and his ascension is a journey of five hundred years, but He completes it in the blink of an eye. That is why God the Almighty said: “In a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years of those which you count. That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.” That is, He directs these affairs, He is a witness to the deeds of His servants. To Him are raised the great and the small, the great and the small. He is the Mighty, who has made everything mighty, so He has subdued and overcome it, and to Him the servants and slaves submit. He is the Merciful to His believing servants, so He is Mighty in His mercy and Merciful in His might.

32:7: God the Almighty says, informing us that He is the One who created all things perfectly, perfected them, and made them perfect. Malik said, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, Who made everything He created perfect, meaning He created everything perfectly, as if He made it from the forefront and the back. Then, when God the Almighty mentioned the creation of the heavens and the earth, He began to mention the creation of man, saying, And He began the creation of man from clay, meaning He created the father of mankind, Adam, from clay. Then He made his descendants from an extract of despised water, meaning they reproduce in the same way from a sperm-drop from between the loins of the man and the ribs of the woman. Then He proportioned him, meaning Adam, when He created him from dust, a sound, upright creation. And breathed into him of His [created] spirit and made for you hearing and sight and hearts, meaning intellects. Little do you give thanks, meaning for these faculties that God the Almighty has given you. So, happy is he who uses them in obedience to his Lord the Almighty.

32:10: God Almighty says, informing us about the polytheists’ rejection of the Resurrection, when they said, If we are lost in the earth, meaning our bodies are torn apart and scattered throughout the earth and gone, Shall we then be in a new creation? meaning, will we return after that state? They enslave that, and this is only far-fetched in relation to their helpless power, not in relation to the power of the One who began them and created them from nothing, whose only command when He wants something is to say to it, Be, and it is. For this reason, the Most High said, Rather, they disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord. Then the Most High said, Say, ‘The Angel of Death who is appointed over you will take you.’ What is apparent from this verse is that the Angel of Death is a specific person from the angels, as is understood from the hadith of al-Bara’ mentioned above in Surat Ibrahim. In some reports, he is called Azrael, and this is the well-known one. Qatadah and others said this, and he has helpers. This is also mentioned in the hadith, that his helpers extract the souls from the rest of the body until they reach the throat and the Angel of Death takes them. Mujahid said, The earth was wrapped up for him and made like a basin from which he could take whenever he wanted. Zuhair ibn Muhammad narrated it in a similar manner from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Yahya ibn Abi Yahya al-Muqri told us, Umar ibn Samurah told us, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father say: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) looked at the Angel of Death at the head of an Ansar man, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: 'O Angel of Death, be gentle with my companion, for he is a believer.' The Angel of Death said: 'O Muhammad, be at ease and be glad, for I am gentle with every believer. Know that there is no house of mud or hair on earth, on land or in the sea, except that I look over them five times a day, to the point that I know their young and old even from their selves. By God, O Muhammad, if I wanted to take the soul of a mosquito, I would not be able to do so until God is the One who gives the command to take it.'" Ja'far said: "I have been informed that he looks over them only at the times of prayer. When death comes to them, if he is one of those who maintain the prayer, the angel approaches him and repels Satan from him, and the angel tells him: 'There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God' in that momentous state." Abdul Razzaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah who said: I heard Mujahid say: There is no house of hair or mud on the face of the earth except that the Angel of Death goes around it twice a day. Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: “By God, there is no house in which there is someone from the people of this world except that the Angel of Death stands at its door seven times a day, checking to see if there is anyone in it whom he has commanded to take his life.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the words of God Almighty: Then to your Lord you will be returned means the Day of your Resurrection and your rising from your graves for your recompense.

32:12: God Almighty tells us about the state of the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection and their words when they witness the resurrection and stand before God Almighty, humble and humiliated, with their heads bowed, that is, out of shame and embarrassment, they say, Our Lord, we have seen and heard, meaning we now hear Your words and obey Your command, as God Almighty said, I will hear them and see them on the Day they come to Us. And they will also blame themselves when they enter the Fire by saying, If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze. And thus these people will say, Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us, that is, to this world, “so that we may do righteousness. Indeed, we are certain,” that is, we have become certain and convinced in it that Your promise is true and that meeting You is true. And God Almighty knew about them that if He returned them to this world, they would be as they were in it, disbelievers who deny the signs of God and disobey His Messengers, as God Almighty said, And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, if only we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord’ [verse]. And He said, Here, And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, as God Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. “But the word from Me will come into effect: ‘I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together,’” meaning of both kinds, for their abode is the Fire, from which they cannot escape nor escape. We seek refuge in God and His perfect words from that. So taste [the punishment] for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours. That is, it will be said to the people of the Fire, by way of rebuke and rebuke: Taste this punishment because of your denial of it, your rejection of its occurrence, and your forgetting it, as you treated it as someone who forgets it. Indeed, We have forgotten you, meaning We will treat you as someone who forgets, because God Almighty does not forget anything and nothing goes astray from Him. Rather, it is by way of reciprocity, as God Almighty said: This Day We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. And God Almighty said: And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do, meaning because of your disbelief and denial, as God Almighty said in the other verse: They will not taste therein coolness or drink, except… “Blood and pus, a just recompense. Indeed, they did not expect an account, and they denied Our signs with utter denial. And all things We have recorded in a book. So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment.”

No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.” Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Harun ibn Ma’ruf and Harun ibn Sa’id, both on the authority of Ibn Wahb on his authority. Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi Omar and others told us, Sufyan told us, Mutraf bin Tarif and Abdul Malik bin Saeed told us, they heard Al-Shaabi narrating on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah who said: “I heard him on the pulpit, attributing it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime: Who is the lowest in status among the people of Paradise? 32:17: God the Almighty says: Only those believe in Our verses meaning only those who believe in them who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration meaning listen to them and obey them in word and deed and exalt the praises of their Lord and are not arrogant meaning they are not proud to follow them and submit to them as the ignorant disbelieving immoral people do. God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell, humbled. Then God the Almighty says: Their sides forsake their beds meaning by that standing in prayer at night, abandoning sleep and lying down on soft mattresses. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said regarding God's statement: Their sides forsake their beds meaning by that standing in prayer at night. Anas, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Al-Munkadir, Abu Hazim and Qatadah said: It is the prayer between the two evening prayers. Anas also said: It is waiting for the evening prayer. Ibn Jarir narrated it with a good chain of narration. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the Isha prayer in congregation and the Fajr prayer in congregation. They call upon their Lord in fear and hope, meaning fear of the consequences of His punishment and hope for His abundant reward. And from what We have provided them, they spend, thus combining the necessary and transitive acts of worship. The leader of these people, their master, and their pride in this world and the hereafter is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Abdullah ibn Rawahah, may God be pleased with him, said. And among us is the Messenger of God reciting his book when the dawn breaks brightly. He showed us guidance after blindness, so our hearts are certain that what he said will come true. He spends the night turning away from his bed when the polytheists make his beds heavy. Imam Ahmad said: Rawh and Affan told us: Hammad ibn Salamah told us: Ata ibn as-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadhani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Our Lord is amazed at two men: a man who rises from his comforter and blanket, from his beloved and his family, to pray. He says: ‘Our Lord, O My angels, look at My servant, he has risen from his bed and comforter, from his beloved and his family, to pray, desiring what is with Me and fearing what is with Me.’ And a man who fights in the cause of God and they are defeated, and He knows what is upon him of fleeing and what is for him in returning, so he returns until his blood is shed, desiring what is with Me and fearing what is with Me. So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, says to the angels: ‘Look at My servant, he has returned desiring what is with Me and fearing what is with Me, until his blood is shed.’” Abu Dawud narrated it in this manner in Jihad on the authority of Musa ibn Ismail on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, with a similar wording. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. One day I was close to him, and we were walking, so I said: ‘O Prophet of God, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me away from Hell.’ He said: ‘You have asked about something great, but it is easy for whomever God makes it easy for: Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, pay zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House.’ Then he said: ‘Shall I not guide you to the gates of goodness? I said: Yes, O Prophet of God. He took hold of my tongue and said: Restrain this. I said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for what we say? He said: May your mother lose you, O Muadh! 32:18: God Almighty tells us about His justice and generosity that He will not treat in His judgment on the Day of Resurrection those who believed in His verses and followed His messengers equally those who were immoral, that is, disobeyed their Lord and denied the messengers of God to him, as God Almighty said: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds - equal in their life and their death? Evil is that which they judge. And God Almighty said: Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption in the land? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked? And God Almighty said: The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise [verse]. That is why God Almighty said here: Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal, that is, before God on the Day of Resurrection. Ata’ ibn Yasar, al-Suddi, and others mentioned that it was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, and that is why He detailed their judgment by saying: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, that is, their hearts believed in the verses of God and they did…” It is required by them, and they are the righteous ones. For them are the Gardens of Refuge, meaning those in which there are dwellings, houses, and lofty rooms. As a lodging, meaning hospitality and honor, “for what they used to do. * But as for those who defiantly disobey,” meaning those who disobeyed, their abode is the Fire. Every time they want to leave it, they are returned to it, like His statement, Every time they want to leave it, out of distress, they are returned to it, the verse. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: By God, their hands are bound, their feet are chained, the flames raise them, and the angels suppress them. And it will be said to them, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ That is, this will be said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke. God the Almighty says: {And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment} Ibn Abbas said: By the lesser punishment, He means the calamities, illnesses, and afflictions of this world, and what befalls its people, as a test by God for His servants so that they may repent to Him. A similar narration was narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Alqama, Atiyah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Abdul-Karim al-Jazari, and Khasif. Ibn Abbas said in a narration from him: It means implementing the prescribed punishments on them. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Mujahid, and Abu 'Ubaidah said: It means the torment of the grave. Al-Nasa'i said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, and Abu 'Ubaidah, from 'Abdullah: {And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment} He said: Years befell them. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Omar Al-Qawariri told me, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Awfi, on the authority of Yahya Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, regarding this verse, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment, he said: The moon and the smoke have passed, and the strike and the binding. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Ibn Mas’ud with a similar chain of transmission. Abdullah bin Mas’ud also said in a narration from him: The lesser punishment was what befell them of killing and captivity on the day of Badr. Malik said the same from Zayd bin Aslam. Al-Suddi and others said: There was not a house in Makkah that was not filled with grief over one of their dead or captured, so they were afflicted or incurred damage, and some of them combined both. God the Almighty said: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them? Meaning, there is no one more unjust than he who is reminded of His verses and made them clear to him, and then after that abandons them, denies them, turns away from them, and forgets them as if he does not know them. Qatada said: Beware of turning away from the remembrance of God, for whoever turns away from His remembrance has been greatly deceived, has fallen into extreme poverty, and has committed one of the greatest sins. For this reason, God the Almighty said, threatening whoever does that: Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals. Meaning, I will take the most severe retribution from whoever does that. Ibn Jarir narrated: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, Muhammad bin Al-Mubarak told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Ubadah bin Nassi, on the authority of Junada bin Abi Umayya, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God say: ‘Three things, whoever does them has committed a sin: whoever ties a banner unjustly, or disobeys his parents, or walks with an oppressor to support him has committed a sin.’ God the Most High says: ‘Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash with this chain of transmission. This is a very strange hadith.

And regarding His words: So be not in doubt about meeting Him, he said: about Moses meeting his Lord, the Almighty. And regarding His words: So be not in doubt about meeting Him, he said: about Moses meeting his Lord, the Almighty. And God Almighty’s words: And We made it, meaning the Book that We gave him, a guidance for the Children of Israel, as God Almighty said in Surat al-Isra’ 17:“And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, saying: ‘Do not take besides Me a protector.’” And His statement: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs. That is, when they were patient in adhering to the commands of God, abandoning His prohibitions, and believing in His messengers and following them in what they brought them, there were leaders among them who guided to the truth by the command of God, and called to good, and enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. Then when they changed, distorted, and interpreted, they were deprived of that status, and their hearts became hardened, distorting words from their places, so there was no righteous action and no correct belief. For this reason, the Most High said: And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture. Qatadah and Sufyan said: When they were patient in refraining from the worldly life. And likewise al-Hasan ibn Salih said. Sufyan said: This is how these people were, and a man should not be an imam to be followed until he avoids the worldly life. Waki’ said: Sufyan said: Religion is indispensable to knowledge, just as the body is indispensable to bread. Ibn Bint Al-Shafi’i said: My father read to my uncle or my uncle read to my father: Sufyan was asked about the statement of Ali may God be pleased with him: Patience is to faith as the head is to the body. Have you not heard His statement, And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient? He said: When they took hold of the head of the matter, they became leaders. Some scholars said: Through patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained. And We gave them clear proofs of the matter” (Al-An’am 2:17), as He said here, Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ, meaning beliefs and deeds.
32:26: God Almighty says: Did not these deniers of the messengers see what God destroyed before them of the past nations because of their denial of the messengers and their opposition to them in what they brought them of the straight paths, so that there remained of them no remnant nor eye nor trace Do you perceive anyone of them or hear a sound of them? That is why He said they walk in their dwellings meaning these deniers walk in the dwellings of those deniers, and they do not see anyone of those who inhabit and develop them, they have gone from them as if they had never prospered in them as He said those are their houses, desolate because of what they did wrong and He said “So how many a town We have destroyed while it was doing wrong, so it is desolate on its roofs, and a well that has been abandoned, and a lofty castle? * Did they not travel through the land and have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? Indeed, it is not eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts.” That is why He said here There are signs in that meaning that in the departure of those people and their destruction and what happened to them Because of their denial of the messengers, and the salvation of those who believed in them, there are signs, lessons, sermons, and similar evidence. Do they not hear, that is, the report of those who came before, how their situation was? And the Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land? God Almighty demonstrates His kindness to His creation and His benevolence towards them in sending water either from the sky or from the flood, which is what rivers carry and descends from the mountains to the lands in need of it at its appropriate times. For this reason, God Almighty said: to the barren land, which is the land in which there is no vegetation, as God Almighty said: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it a barren plain, meaning dry land that does not grow anything. What is meant by His saying to the barren land is not only the land of Egypt, but it is part of what is meant, even though many commentators have used it as an example. It is not the only intended meaning, but it is certainly what is meant by this verse, for it is in itself a soft, rough land that needs water, and if it rained on it, its buildings would collapse. So God Almighty drives the Nile to it with what it can carry of the increase resulting from the rains of the land of Abyssinia, and in it is red clay, so it covers the land of Egypt, which is a salty, sandy land in need of that water and that clay as well, so that the crops grow in it, and they exploit new water every year. Rain in a country other than theirs, and new clay from a land other than theirs, so glory be to the Wise, the Generous, the Gracious, the Praiseworthy forever. Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Qais bin Hajjaj on the authority of someone who told him: When Egypt was conquered, its people came to Amr bin Al-Aas, when he entered Bu’una, one of the months of the Persians, and they said: O Prince, our Nile has a law that it does not flow except according to it. He said: What is that? They said: Twelve nights have passed of this month, so we took a virgin girl between her parents, and satisfied her parents, and put the best jewelry and clothes on her, then we threw her into this Nile. Amr said to them: This will not happen in Islam, Islam destroys what came before it. They stayed for a while and the Nile was not flowing until they were about to leave. Amr wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab about that, and Umar wrote back to him: You have done well by what you did, and I have sent you a card inside this letter of mine, so throw it into the Nile. When his letter was delivered, Amr took the card and opened it, and it said: From the servant of God, Umar, Commander of the Faithful, to the Nile of the people of Egypt. As for what follows, if it flows from you, then it will not flow. If it is God, the One, the Compeller, who is the One who flows you, then we ask God to flow you. He said: So he threw the card into the Nile and they woke up on Saturday and God had made the Nile flow sixteen cubits in one night. God has stopped that tradition from the people of Egypt until today. It was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Lalakai Al-Tabari in his book, Al-Sunnah. That is why God Almighty said: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and themselves eat? Then will they not see? Just as God Almighty said: “So let man look at his food. * How We poured down water in torrents.” That is why He said here: Then will they not see? Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, to the barren land, he said: It is the land that receives nothing but rain that does not avail it at all except what comes to it from torrents. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: It is a land in Yemen. And Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: It is villages between Yemen and Syria. And Ikrimah, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: The barren land is the one in which there is no vegetation, and it is dusty. I said: This is like the statement of God, the Most High, “And a sign for them is the dead land. We have given it life” Al-Anfal 2:17.

32:28: God the Almighty says, informing about the disbelievers' haste and the occurrence of God's punishment upon them, and the descent of His wrath and punishment upon them, out of estrangement, denial and stubbornness, And they say, 'When will this conquest be?' That is, when will you be victorious over us, O Muhammad? Just as you claim that you have a time against us and that you will be avenged from us, so when will this be? We do not see you and your companions except hiding, fearful and humiliated. God the Almighty says, Say, 'On the Day of Conquest,' That is, when God's punishment, wrath and anger descend upon you in this world and the next, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieve, nor will they be reprieved. As God the Almighty says, But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge. The two verses. Whoever claims that what is meant by this conquest is the conquest of Mecca has gone too far, made a mistake, and is very blatant. On the day of the conquest, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted the conversion of the freed slaves, and they were close to two thousand. If what was meant was the conquest of Mecca, he would not have accepted their conversion, because God Almighty said: Say, on the Day of Conquest, ‘The faith of those who disbelieve will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.’ Rather, what is meant is the conquest, which is judgment and separation, like His saying: Then judge between me and them with a conquest 17:20, and His saying: Say, ‘Our Lord will bring us together, then judge between us with truth’ 17:20. God Almighty said: And they sought victory, but every obstinate tyrant was disappointed. God Almighty said: And before, they used to ask for victory against those who disbelieved. God Almighty said: If you ask for victory, victory has already come to you. Then God the Almighty said: {So turn away from them and wait, for indeed, they are waiting.} That is, turn away from these polytheists, and convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, as He says: {Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no deity except Him.} And wait, for God will fulfill what He promised and will grant you victory over those who disobey you. Indeed, He does not break His promise. And His statement, {Indeed, they are waiting.} That is, you are waiting, and they are waiting, and they are awaiting misfortunes for you. {Or do they say, He is a poet for whom we are awaiting a misfortune of time?} And you will see the consequences of your patience with them and of carrying out God’s message in granting you victory and support, and they will find after what they are awaiting in you and your companions the severe punishment of God for them, and the descent of His torment upon them. God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The last interpretation of Surat As-Sajdah, praise and thanks be to God.
